prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Make one heritage atlas plate. IMAGE 1 is ONLY the Longmen thin-black-line STYLE master; following photographs determine this subject's geometry, NOT their scene. Draw fine sparse BLACK contours, deliberately simplified joints, a few selected roof/stone detail lines. Every non-ink pixel inside and outside the object is perfectly flat opaque PURE WHITE #FFFFFF. No filled black shadows, grayscale, hatching, color, paper grain, gradient, glow, checkerboard, frame, caption, watermark or lettering. Plaques remain blank. Remove tourists, modern fences, cables, trees, sky, paving, other buildings and all ground shadows. Full uncut subject, apex and own base intact, centered with at least 8% clear margins. This is a faithful present-object illustration, not a speculative reconstruction.

Subject is Dazheng Hall at Shenyang Imperial Palace, present OCTAGONAL pavilion-shaped main hall, not Beijing Forbidden City. Near-frontal shallow perspective from PHOTO2. EXACTLY TWO octagonal eave levels with a pointed pyramidal canopy, single ornate apex, no hip-roof ridge or gables. Preserve actual front paired carved dragon-wrapped posts, red-post geometry, deeply layered but sparsely outlined bracket bands, paneled doors, and complete pale-stone raised terrace with front steps and balustrades. PHOTO3 is only actual weathered bracket DETAIL, not another building. Width about75% of landscape1536x1024.
